target.title: Drop redundant escaping in redirect
target.description: The location is already URL-encoded with iri_to_uri when the Location header is set, so escaping it again for the HTML body is redundant.

summary: Remove redundant escaping of the location string in the HTML body of redirect responses.

suspects.title: Unescaped location in HTML body could lead to XSS

text:
Investigate this suspected problem.

Suspect S1: Unescaped location in HTML body could lead to XSS
Category: security
Location: src/werkzeug/utils.py lines 260-260 (new version)
Suspected problem: Removing escape(location) means that if the Location header contains characters like quotes or angle brackets (even if URL encoded, or if iri_to_uri does not encode certain characters like single quotes depending on version/context), injecting raw location values into the HTML attribute href="..." could result in XSS.
What would confirm or refute it: Check how iri_to_uri behaves with malicious inputs, and whether other places in the codebase escape URL strings before putting them into HTML attribute contexts.

The planner's summary of the pull request: Remove redundant escaping of the location string in the HTML body of redirect responses.

arguments.suggested_fix: Restore html_location = escape(location) before embedding it in the response HTML template.
arguments.explanation: Removing escape(location) from `redirect()` in src/werkzeug/utils.py causes the location string to be embedded directly into the HTML response body's `<a href="...">` attribute without HTML escaping. If a malicious or crafted location header contains quotes or angle brackets, an attacker can break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (XSS) when a user visits the fallback redirect page.
